basis: Growth hormone resistance defines endocrine dysfunction; immune dysregulation is a defining component.
Premature fusion of one cranial suture; neurologic damage is not inherent to isolated unisutural craniosynostosis.
Skin disease and neurodegeneration define XP/CS; retinopathy/optic atrophy and hearing loss occur in 80-99%; arteriosclerosis (80-99%) omitted by cap.
Usually infectious inflammation of the epididymis and testes; reproductive anatomy has no organ axis.
Carcinoma originates in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes; spread is not assumed.
Combined pituitary hormone deficiencies; seizures in 1/2 may accompany hypoglycemia and do not establish intrinsic neurologic damage.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration; hearing, cognitive and gonadal annotations lack frequencies supporting common involvement.
Urea-cycle/ammonia detoxification disorder; encephalopathy and hepatic dysfunction are common (~30%+), with frequency varying across subtypes.
Inflammation of subcutaneous fat; the umbrella does not establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Storage disease with neurodegeneration and ichthyosis; visual impairment 80-99%; skeletal disease and hearing loss (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Severe intellectual disability and epilepsy define the syndrome; recurrent infections (30-79%) do not establish intrinsic immunodeficiency.
Childhood cerebral calcification; supplied Aicardi-Goutieres and inborn-error-of-immunity ancestry supports an immune-mediated neurologic disorder.
Cordylobia larvae infest skin and produce furuncular lesions.
Immune-mediated medium-vessel vasculitis; transient mucocutaneous findings, reactive blood counts and proteinuria do not establish additional organ damage.
Coagulation disorder explicitly defined here by excessive thrombus formation in vessels; no downstream organ infarction is assumed.
Allergic hypersensitivity to ragweed; sensitivity alone does not establish airway or ocular damage.
Inherited susceptibility defined by intracerebral hemorrhage as its target; actual hemorrhage or additional organ damage is not established.
Facial skeletal dysostosis, ocular defects and oral clefts define the disorder; corneal opacity and cleft/dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%; cognitive impairment is under 30%.
Congenital hand or foot skeletal malformation with supernumerary digits; associated anomalies are not inherent.
Neurodevelopmental and ocular defects with hypogonadism define syndrome; joint stiffness/contractures occur in 80-99% and kyphoscoliosis in 30-79%.
Developmental absence of portions of the retina and choroid, usually impairing vision.
Bacterial pus accumulation, usually occupying the pleural space; nonpleural subtypes do not justify additional axes across the umbrella.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in the small intestine; lymphoma also receives the immune mechanism axis.
Capillary barrier dysfunction; pulmonary edema (30-79%) often reflects fluid resuscitation/recruitment; pancreatitis is separately diagnosed; renal injury is under 30%.
Pachygyria, arachnoid cysts, intellectual disability and epilepsy define a neurologic disorder; skeletal involvement lacks supporting frequency.
